extracted.intended_audience: self-published, indie, and unpublished authors seeking a paid Kirkus Indie book review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation standards for submitting a book to Kirkus Indie (paid review service), including how reviews are assigned, what reviewers assess, formatting/submission requirements, review lengths/turnaround, publication/excerpting rules, and options for publishing or keeping reviews private.

rubrics_metrics.name: How Kirkus chooses a reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: A Kirkus editor analyzes your book and considers elements such as content, style, genre, and sub-genre. We then match your book with a reviewer who is a content and genre expert, has experience with similar styles, and enjoys books like yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors assign titles based on a reviewer's professional experience, expertise, and reading interests. Reviewers include librarians, business executives, journalists from national publications, PhDs in religion and literature, creative executives, and other professional reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment basis — merit judged on content and reading experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Our professional reviewers assess merit based on the value of the content and reading experience alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover design, marketing plan, format (e-book vs. print), and other collateral do not affect the reviewer’s merit assessment. Reviews are intended to evaluate work's value and potential in the marketplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest and impartial evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Indie reviewers are experienced professionals who honestly and impartially evaluate the books they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews can be positive (even earning a Kirkus Star), negative, or anywhere in between. What is guaranteed is a fair, unbiased assessment. Authors may keep negative reviews private and use them as feedback to improve their craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary content is fundamental
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary content is a fundamental element of Kirkus' reviews, because Kirkus aims to help consumers, booksellers, librarians, publishers, agents, movie producers, and other influencers discover new books and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews include enough summary content to give context to criticism and help readers decide if the book will be of interest to them; across all sections reviews include significant summary plus professional opinion-based analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review lengths by option
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional Reviews: 250 words. Expanded Review: About 500 words. Picture Book: 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each option lists pricing and standard turnaround; expedited options are available at higher prices (examples given: Traditional expedited $599, Expanded expedited $750, Picture Book expedited $450).

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround times / due dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If you order standard service, the review will be returned within 7-9 weeks of the date we receive your submission. If you order express service, you will receive the review within 4-6 weeks of the date we receive your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirkus calculates due dates based on the receipt date of submission and will email to confirm receipt and the due date. After the review is ready an author dashboard link is emailed for download.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication control / confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: You may choose to publish your review on KirkusReviews.com where it can be discovered by industry influencers... If you receive a negative review, you can choose NOT to publish your review and it will never see the light of day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors decide whether to publish reviews on Kirkus.com; unpublished reviews remain private and can be used only for personal feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for magazine and newsletter is editorially discretionary
rubrics_metrics.description: Our editors select about 40 reviews to feature in each issue of the magazine... The selections are 100 percent at the editors' discretion, and they typically choose the strongest reviews in a variety of genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors also choose one Indie review to feature in each edition of the email newsletter. Selection criteria are editorial discretion focused on strength and genre variety; there is no guarantee of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kirkus Star visibility and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you choose to publish your review on the Kirkus website, you will see whether your book earned a Kirkus Star. If your book does receive a Star, it will immediately be eligible for the Kirkus Prize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page does not specify exact criteria for awarding a Kirkus Star, only that published reviews will show Star status and make the book eligible for prizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting preferences (does not affect review outcome)
rubrics_metrics.description: We will accept PDF and Word documents with any formatting. Formatting does not affect the result of the review, but here are our preferences: Font: 12-point Times New Roman; Margins: 1 inch all around; Spacing: 1.5- or double-spaced; Page numbers: Bottom of page, centered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a polished, final version of your book (including illustrations, if applicable). Reviewers will treat any title they receive as a finished work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final manuscript requirement / no post-submission changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit a final version of your manuscript when placing your order. We will not be able to accommodate any manuscript changes once the book has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submitted file is the finished work; include illustrations where applicable because reviewers will evaluate the submitted version as final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series recommendation — submit the first title
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly recommend that authors submit the first title in a given series so that our Indie reviewers can have the full context for the story or subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing the series first volume gives reviewers necessary context to assess story arcs and characters; this is a recommendation, not a strict requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to request the same reviewer for subsequent books
rubrics_metrics.description: If you were pleased with your first review, you may request to have the same reviewer read your next book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirkus cannot guarantee the same reviewer will be available; requests are honored when possible but are not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial style includes reference to previous works
rubrics_metrics.description: It is Kirkus’ editorial style to refer to an author's previous work. We include this information to give readers additional context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should expect reviews may mention an author's past titles to situate the new work for readers; this is consistent editorial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excerpting policy — full publication on Kirkus required before excerpts
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews acquired through the Kirkus Indie program must be published in their entirety on Kirkus.com before any portion of the reviews are published (online or in print) for any use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must post the complete review to Kirkus.com prior to excerpting lines elsewhere; a separate excerpting guideline page provides full rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications and pool size
rubrics_metrics.description: Our indie reviews are written by qualified professionals, such as librarians, nationally published journalists, creative executives and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirkus Indie works with approximately 200 reviewers across varied professional backgrounds to cover many genres and subject areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: No restriction on publication date for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus Indie does not put any restrictions on publication dates for submissions. You may order a review for a book that's been on the market for 10 years or for a book that doesn't even have a publication date yet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy aims to introduce consumers and industry influencers to self-published books they might otherwise never discover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and licensing of reviews to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews will be included in content feeds, which are sent to more than 20 licensees, such as BN.com, Google Books, Ingram, Baker & Taylor, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are sent to BN.com within two weeks of their publication on the Kirkus website, but third-party sites control timing and whether they publish the review. To post on Amazon, authors must contact an Amazon representative directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted formats and language scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Kirkus accepts e-book format (they assess content reading experience) and reviews Spanish-language books, but they do not review audiobooks in any format and do not offer reviews of books in other languages at this time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit in PDF or Word (or accepted e-book form for content review). Non-Spanish foreign-language books are not accepted under current policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may order through Indie program
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you are not self-published, you may order a review through the Indie program. This is common for authors whose publishers missed the galley submission deadline, whose books did not fall into the categories reviewed through our traditional program, or whose books simply weren't slated for review due to the volume of submissions our editors receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is open to self-published and traditionally published authors who missed other submission routes; there is no strict limitation to only self-published authors.
